key_insight: Quantum error correction does not remove relativistic time dilation; instead, the proper-time difference between two protected memories emerges as a relational logical phase when they are compared.
engineering_relevance: This suggests fault-tolerant quantum memories can act as robust relativistic clocks, enabling long-coherence timing experiments and deterministic logical gates from controlled proper-time excursions.
method: Analyze two error-corrected quantum memories on distinct worldlines with local references
Show the local correction histories factor exactly from the proper-time difference
Demonstrate that at code-admitted phases the relational evolution becomes a deterministic logical gate, including an S-type Clifford at a c0/2 excursion
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a theoretical derivation with exact factorization and code-consistent phase-gate behavior, rather than an empirical benchmark or dataset.
watch_item: The result is idealized and depends on locally referenced control and code-specific phase conditions, so experimental realization may be sensitive to timing, synchronization, and hardware noise.
paper_title: Quantum Error-Corrected Memories Keep Proper Time
